title: Per-chunk span correlation and PII-aware sanitization for streaming API
creator: Asha Menon
description: Add deterministic per-chunk telemetry and tracing for streamed responses while ensuring PII is sanitized before it reaches logs/metrics. This ticket implements: (1) chunk identifiers and light-weight headers propagated from API gateway through runtime so traces across reconnects and retries can be correlated; (2) span lifecycle semantics for a streaming response (initial request span, per-chunk child spans, finalization span) compatible with existing OpenTelemetry pipelines; (3) a PII-aware sanitization stage that runs before any chunk is emitted to observability backends and before structured logging; (4) a compatibility shim so existing customers using OpenAI-style SSE semantics see identical behavior and mapping of chunks to messages; (5) rollout and sampling strategy to limit telemetry volume for high-throughput routes and a feature flag for immediate rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic chunk_id attached to every chunk event and present in request/response logs
Trace contains a parent request span and one child span per delivered chunk with timing and token_count attributes
Sanitization pipeline removes or masks configured PII patterns (emails, credit-cards, SSNs) before metrics/log exports
Compatibility shim maps chunk events to OpenAI SSE 'delta' messages for customers using that compatibility mode
End-to-end tests that validate span correlation across reconnects and server-side retries
Performance regression <5% p99 latency impact on streaming endpoint in canary tests
tasks: Design chunk_id format and propagation: deterministic, 128-bit hex + sequence (A.Menon)
Implement tracing hooks in runtime: create parent span, emit child spans per chunk (D.Ramirez)
Implement PII-sanitizer module with configurable regex rules and allowlist/denylist (SRE)
Add compatibility shim for OpenAI-style streaming in SDK layer (SDK team)
Instrument sampling controls and feature flag (config-service)
Write unit tests and integration harness using local streaming emulator
Prepare canary rollout plan and dashboard widgets for per-route chunk metrics
comments: 2026-03-10 Asha Menon: Initial ticket created after postmortem for STREAM-INCIDENT-2026-02. We need to stop leaking raw chunk text to logs and make traces queryable by chunk_id.

2026-03-11 Diego Ramirez: Spike completed — prototype attaches chunk_id at gateway and persists it in the runtime request context. Found race when reconnects reuse session_id; will include seq_num to disambiguate. Notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STREAM/Chunk+ID+Design
2026-03-12 Priya Patel (Security): Reviewed sanitization approach. Recommend layered approach: regex masks then ML-based detector for obfuscated PII. Security review required before canary.

2026-03-12 Diego Ramirez: Opened PR #1024 with tracing hooks and in-memory sanitizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1024 — basic tests passing. Need SRE to review performance implications.
2026-03-13 SRE (Ben Cox): Load test w/ sampling=0.1 shows 3% p99 increase. Suggest default sampling 0.05 for high-throughput routes and sample=1 for routes with explicit debug flag.

2026-03-14 Asha Menon: Merged design doc into confluence, created dashboard template for chunk-level latency and token distribution. Plan: start canary 2026-03-16 for one beta customer route. (Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/chunk-metrics)
notes: Rollout plan: gated by feature flag + telemetry sampling. Step 1: internal canary (dev+staging). Step 2: Beta customer route (1 tenant) at 10% traffic. Step 3: 50% traffic. Step 4: global default with sampling threshold adjusted.

PII ruleset: start with conservative masks for emails and credit-cards. Add ML detector after initial canary. Keep sanitized raw_text out of metrics but allow hashed fingerprint for de-duplication analysis.
Compatibility: SDK shim will translate our chunk events into OpenAI SSE 'delta' + 'role' messages; document mapping in SDK release notes. Ensure customer feature flag to opt-in/opt-out.
Observability cost: expected additional ingest ~0.8% of total token events at sampling 5%. We must add quota guard to avoid bill shock.
